newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore judge stays massive Barings lawsuit.
newsitem.headline: Singapore judge stays massive Barings lawsuit.

text.p: A Singapore high court judge on Thursday ordered a stay in a Singapore $2 billion (US$1.4 billion) negligence lawsuit against the auditors of Baring Futures (Singapore) (BFS).
Justice Lai Kew Chai agreed to defending firm Deloitte & Touche Singapore's application that the suit by BFS' liquidators be stayed.
His decision came after arguments by Haridass Ajaib, lawyer for Deloitte & Touche, that the suit should not proceed in Singapore because the principal players in the Barings collapse were in England.

"In the interests of all parties and for the ends of justice, England is the proper forum where all principal players are brought together and can be compelled and where the responsibility for this disaster can be ascertained and liability distributed between those concerned," Haridass said.
There was no immediate indication whether lawyers for the liquidators would appeal the stay, which suspends Singapores proceedings.
BFS is the Barings subsidiary in which jailed rogue trader Nick Leeson chalked up US$1.4 billion of losses in unauthorised derivative deals which broke the bank last year.
Deloitte & Touche Singapore were the external auditors of BFS since its incorporation in 1986 until end 1993 when they were replaced by Coopers & Lybrand Singapore.
Both companies are being sued by the Barings administrators in London as well as by the BFS liquidators.
Partners of audit firm Price Waterhouse acted as inspectors of BFS and are currently its liquidators.
Barings adminstrators in London filed separate claims earlier this year in London against Coopers & Lybrand and Deloitte & Touche units.
The administrators said then that the size of the claims was substantial, but they did not indicate a dollar amount.
